clue.text: Dull part of cricket pitch

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end in cricket
to pitch is to throw, as is to cast

explanation.surface: A grumble about a lifeless stretch of turf on a cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like the cricket strip, but here it is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is grey and cloudy, so the day is dull.

clue.text: Regarding enemy rising loudly and unmatched

parts.note: on means regarding, about

indicators.note: rising in a down answer means the word enemy's synonym is read upwards

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
F, forte, is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: An unrivalled foe climbing up and shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns FOE into EOF, read upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off is unique, with nothing else to match or equal it.

clue.text: Seaplane crashed across end of Southwold promenade

indicators.note: across says the scrambled letters span the other letter, enclosing it
crashed suggests the word seaplane is wrecked into a new order
end of picks the last letter of Southwold

explanation.surface: A seaplane comes down over a seafront in Southwold, a Suffolk seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' rearranges SEAPLANE; 'across' puts it around D, the end of Southwold.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a level public walkway, usually along a seafront.

clue.text: Shy laugh the French dismissed

indicators.note: dismissed says one word is sent away from the other

parts.note: a chuckle is a quiet laugh
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: A timid giggle brushed off by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' reads as timid but is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy is to throw something, as at a coconut shy; chuck is a synonym.

clue.text: Secret agent skins up with little sign of hesitation

indicators.note: up in a down answer says the word for skins is read upwards

parts.note: peels means skins, as with fruit
er is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: A spy rolls a joint, hesitating slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is a spy planted long in advance and left inactive until needed.

clue.text: Functional uniform with fur

parts.note: Uniform is the radio alphabet word for U
sable is a prized dark fur from a small mammal

explanation.surface: A practical uniform trimmed with fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Something functional works and can be put to use, which is a synonym sense.

clue.text: Bores quit changing nickname

indicators.note: changing says the letters of bores quit swap around

explanation.surface: Tedious people giving up a different name for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobriquet is an affectionate or descriptive name, a synonym for nickname.

clue.text: Sword turned up in pedal bin

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the words pedal bin

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A weapon found tossed upside-down in the kitchen bin.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden step no indicator; 'in' is that indicator, so it is added. 'turned up' reads the letters upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade is a poetic word for a sword, part standing for the whole weapon.

clue.text: Approved of final section by journalist written about Old Republican

indicators.note: written about says the first pieces are set down around the others

parts.note: the final part is the end
ED, short for editor, is crossword shorthand for a journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist's closing paragraph praising an elderly politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' is the containment signal: the journalist's pieces are written around the old Republican. S for section is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to give backing, literally signing the back of a document as approval.

clue.text: Embraced sixth sense love employed

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is called the sixth sense
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
employed means used

explanation.surface: Someone took up their intuition, love and work all together.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to adopt or take it up, as one embraces an idea.

clue.text: American directors on ship

parts.note: a company's directors together form its board

explanation.surface: US company bosses are travelling by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aboard means being on a vessel as passenger or crew.

clue.text: Heartless cook behind house wine

indicators.note: behind says the cook piece follows the house piece
heartless says the inner letters of cook are cut out

explanation.surface: A gutless chef lurks at the back of a house with wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is the British name for German white wine from the Rhine.

clue.text: Fine, limp fringe

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
lank hair hangs limp and lifeless

explanation.surface: A hair verdict: the fringe is fine but hangs limp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fringe' tempts as a haircut, but it is the definition in its sense of an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A flank is the side or edge of something, its outer margin.

clue.text: Exploit Oscar during unusual free trip

indicators.note: during says one letter sits within the other letters
unusual tells us the words free trip are put into an odd order

parts.note: Oscar is the radio alphabet word for O

explanation.surface: Taking advantage of a perk: a free trip with an Oscar winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns FREE TRIP into PRFITEER, and 'during' puts O inside it after PR.
explanation.definitionFit: To profiteer is to make excessive gains by exploiting scarcity or circumstance.

clue.text: One suspended in hot incense

parts.note: H is the tap abbreviation for hot
to incense someone is to anger them

explanation.surface: A person hanging amid fragrant smoke from burning incense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incense' looks like the fragrance but is the verb meaning to enrage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that hangs, such as a pendant or decoration, is a hanger.

clue.text: Supplies reportedly more disgusting diners regularly

indicators.note: reportedly says we want a word that is heard like another

parts.note: grosser means more disgusting

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of diners, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A news item on nastier restaurant patrons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes IES, the even letters of diners.
explanation.definitionFit: Groceries are food and household provisions, the supplies one shops for.

clue.text: Endlessly lucky Ken rolled joint

indicators.note: rolled says these letters are tumbled into a fresh order
endlessly says the final letter of lucky is dropped

explanation.surface: A fortunate man named Ken rolled himself a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' trims LUCKY to LUCK; 'rolled' scrambles LUCK and KEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A knuckle is a finger joint, so the answer is an example of a joint.

clue.text: Stand after knock out in the manner of Australian native

indicators.note: after says the word for stand follows the other pieces

parts.note: KO is short for knockout in boxing
a la is French for in the style of
to bear is to stand or tolerate

explanation.surface: An Aussie boxer gets up after a knockout, like an Australian native.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala is an animal native to Australia, often loosely called a koala bear.

clue.text: Dim foe I'd routed changed

indicators.note: routed hints at a defeated army scattered, so the letters are broken up

explanation.surface: A stupid enemy that I defeated was transformed.
explanation.definitionFit: Modified means altered or adjusted, a synonym for changed.

clue.text: Demanding individual run out by you and I

parts.note: an individual is one
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O stands for out, as on a scoreboard or in electronics
you and I together are us

explanation.surface: A cricket complaint: a pushy player got run out because of the pair of us.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous task is burdensome, demanding much effort.

clue.text: Part of nourishing piece of beef

indicators.note: part of says the answer lies within the word nourishing

explanation.surface: A cut of beef that forms part of a nutritious meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Shin is a cut of beef from the lower leg, used for stewing.

clue.text: A small platter is out of place

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a platter is a large flat serving tray

explanation.surface: A little serving dish has been put down in the wrong spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone astray has wandered from its proper position or is lost.

clue.text: Club succeeded in promotion of street artist

indicators.note: in says one letter goes within the other pieces
promotion raises things, so in a down answer the letters run upwards

parts.note: a lane is a narrow street
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A club did well in promoting a street artist.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'promotion of' lifts the street and artist upwards, and 'in' lodges the succeeded letter among them. RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a London football club.

clue.text: Pelt across right bend in piste

indicators.note: across says the first word stretches over the other letters

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's skin
a U-bend is a pipe bend shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: An animal hide lies over a right-hand turn on the slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like a verb to rush, but it is an animal's hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste is a prepared slope or trail for skiing.

clue.text: Profanities as naughty child draws across middle of frieze

indicators.note: across says the first pieces stretch over the central letters, holding them

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
draws in sport are ties

indicators.note: middle of picks the central two letters of frieze

explanation.surface: A rude child scrawls swear words over a decorative frieze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' means the child and draws straddle the centre of frieze, which 'middle of' supplies as two letters since frieze has six.
explanation.definitionFit: Impieties are irreverent acts or words, so profanities are examples of them.

clue.text: Leapt around in coat

indicators.note: around says the letters of leapt are moved about

explanation.surface: Someone jumped about wearing a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To plate is to coat a metal with a thin layer of another, such as gold or silver.

clue.text: Golf shot starts to spin hard after nasty knock

indicators.note: starts to says the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A golfer's ball spins badly after being struck awkwardly.
explanation.definitionFit: A shank is a mishit in golf, struck off the heel of the club.

clue.text: Avoid drink in street

indicators.note: in says the drink goes within the abbreviation

parts.note: kir is a drink of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: A warning to steer clear of drinking out on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt an issue is to go round it rather than face it, evading it.

clue.text: Emphatic type with male mice hearts

indicators.note: hearts means the central letters of each of the words are taken

explanation.surface: A strangely forceful sort of creature, with brave male mice at its core.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic typeface slants letters and is used for emphasis in print.

clue.text: Manipulate mechanic?

definitions.meaning: to ... an outcome is to contrive or manipulate it
a skilled mechanic who maintains machines

explanation.definitionFit: The same word serves as a verb for contriving and a noun for a technician.

clue.text: Elegant and witty, eases oddly inside

indicators.note: inside says these letters go within the other word

parts.note: dry humour is understated wit

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of eases

explanation.surface: A person who is stylish and clever puts others at their ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the first, third and fifth letters of eases, and 'inside' places them within the word for witty.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy clothes are smart and stylish, fit for a formal occasion.

clue.text: Pressing item is dull and inflexible

parts.note: flat means dull or lacking interest
iron as an adjective means unyielding, inflexible

explanation.surface: An urgent matter turns out to be boring and rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' suggests urgent, but it means ironing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatiron is an old-fashioned iron heated on a stove to press laundry.
